candidate_relations.reason: Hypothyroidism is a distinct diagnosis and does not identify brown bowel syndrome from vitamin E deficiency and intestinal lipofuscin deposition.
Whipple disease is a distinct infectious enteropathy; the record and benchmark specify brown bowel syndrome.
Intestinal pseudo-obstruction describes the recurrent nonmechanical obstructive presentation but omits the specific diagnosis of brown bowel syndrome.
Mechanical obstruction was considered, but exploratory laparotomy found no mechanical cause; it is not the benchmark diagnosis.
Scleroderma can cause intestinal dysmotility but is a distinct disease and is not supported as the cause here.
Amyloidosis is a separate infiltrative disorder and does not denote brown bowel syndrome.
Cronkhite-Canada syndrome is a distinct polyposis and malabsorption disorder, not brown bowel syndrome.

Brown bowel syndrome produces an acquired visceral smooth-muscle myopathy from lipofuscin accumulation, but 'visceral myopathy' omits the specific vitamin E deficiency-associated brown bowel diagnosis.

case_quality_flags: The supplied excerpt lacks histologic confirmation of intestinal lipofuscin deposition, although the benchmark diagnosis is explicit.
